links.outcome: Errors introduced by LLM when converting psychiatric notes into patient-facing text
links.effect: Five categories of clinically relevant errors identified (clinical misinterpretation, attribution, content distortion, abbreviation/terminology, structural/syntax) despite improved readability; errors described as prevalent.
links.quote: However, critical errors remain prevalent and can impair clinical judgment, understanding of patient circumstances, clarity of medication regimens, and interpretation of clinical observations.

links.outcome: Errors in AI-transformed clinical notes that would reach patients without clinician review
links.effect: Five categories of clinically relevant errors found in LLM-revised notes, including misrepresentation of suicidality assessments; authors conclude clinician oversight is essential.
links.quote: To safely integrate artificial intelligence-generated documentation into psychiatric care, clinician oversight and targeted model refinement are essential.

screen.reason: Empirical qualitative safety and error evaluation of GPT-3.5 Turbo transforming psychiatric clinical notes into patient-centered text. It evaluates the raw model's safety/errors rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
